records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:37 — Pagination permits concurrent requests without request ordering or an in-flight guard, so a slower earlier response can overwrite the members and offset from a later click.
records.rationale: The next/previous actions in admin-group.js.es6 set offset and call group.findMembers() (which issues an async ajax call and setProperties on resolution) with no in-flight guard or request-ordering; a slower earlier response can indeed overwrite members/offset from a later click. This race is introduced by the diff's new pagination logic.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:56 — The new add/remove actions discard rejected mutation promises and provide no failure feedback, leaving admins unable to tell that the membership change failed.
records.rationale: The diff verifiably shows addMembers/removeMember in admin-group.js.es6 call this.get('model').addMembers(...) / removeMember(member) and discard the returned promises, and model.addMembers/removeMember in group.js only reload members in .then handlers — so on failure the member list is never refreshed and no error feedback is shown. Adding nonexistent usernames or failing server calls silently leaves stale UI, which is a real behavioral gap introduced by this change.

records.rationale: The admin group controller is a singleton in Ember; setupController only sets model (controller.set("model", model)) and never resets usernames. addMembers calls this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames")) using the stale usernames string, and the diff itself contains a TODO acknowledging the input is not cleared. So text entered for a previously viewed group could be added to the new group on clicking Add.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — Removing the sole member on the last page reloads with the stale offset and leaves the admin on an empty page.
records.rationale: The diff shows removeMember() in group.js calls self.findMembers() after the DELETE, but user_count is only updated from the server response (result.meta.total) and offset is clamped via Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0)) using the stale pre-removal user_count. If the removed member was the only one on the last page, the stale user_count keeps offset beyond the new total, so the reload can return an empty member list and currentPage/totalPages stay inconsistent until a server response corrects them.

records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:31 — Concurrent page requests blindly overwrite shared pagination state, so out-of-order responses can display the wrong page.
records.rationale: In group.js, findMembers issues an ajax request and its .then unconditionally setProperties({user_count, limit, offset, members}) from the response. next/previous actions set offset and call findMembers without aborting prior in-flight requests, so out-of-order responses would overwrite shared pagination state and render the wrong page. The mechanism is visible in the diff; it is a real (if low-severity) concurrency defect, though likelihood of user-triggered interleaving is moderate.
